personality_one_liner: A premium, trustworthy, and rugged outdoor utility that guides serious anglers with crisp data and earthy warmth.

spacing.rule: Generous iOS-native padding. Group related data tightly, but leave plenty of breathing room between sections for outdoor legibility.

do's: Use on the bottom tab bar when content scrolls behind.
Use as a frosted overlay on the Today screen's hero background.
Use on floating action buttons (Log Catch) paired with a brandTertiary tint.
dont's: Do not use on regular data cards or forecast lists.
Do not use over dense text sections.

screens.name: Today
screens.purpose: A dashboard presenting the fishing score, critical weather elements, and a barometric pressure trend to determine if today is a good day to fish.

states.empty: N/A - Weather data is always present, if location fails show 'Enable Location'.
states.error: Readable message ('Unable to fetch conditions') with a Retry button.

screens.layout: Header: Location name (left), Spots and Settings icons (right). Main Hero: Large featured card with a 'golden hour water' background image overlaid with a glassmorphism panel. The panel houses a prominent Fishing Score (circular gauge or large typography) and verdict (Excellent/Fair/Poor). Below hero: A 2-column grid of modular cards for Barometric Pressure (showing rising/falling arrow), Wind/Temp, and Solunar Periods. Bottom: A full-width 'AI Almanac' card offering local tips.

screens.name: Forecast
screens.purpose: 7-day outlook to help anglers plan their next trip.
screens.layout: Vertical list of cards. Each row contains the Date, a color-coded Fishing Score badge (Moss for Good, Terracotta for Poor), High/Low temps, and a brief condition summary. Tapping a day expands to show a horizontal hourly scroll of activity levels.

screens.name: Fish
screens.purpose: A catalog of seasonal fish species currently available in the local area.

states.empty: Illustration of a fishing rod with 'No local species data'.

screens.layout: Multi-column grid (2-col). Each card contains a real transparent PNG of the fish on a surfaceSecondary background, Species Name, and tags for Best Time (Dawn/Dusk). High visual appeal to motivate the angler.

screens.name: Log
screens.purpose: Personal catch journal to record photos, species, size, and conditions.

states.empty: Silhouette of a fisherman with 'Your catch journal is empty. Log your first catch!'.

screens.layout: Vertical feed of stacked cards. Each card acts as a memory: full-width catch photo on top, protected by a dark gradient scrim at the bottom where the species name and weight are overlaid in white. Below the photo, a compact row detailing the location and weather conditions at the time of catch. A sticky FAB (glassmorphism) floats at the bottom right to 'Add Catch'.

hero_background.alt: Rippling water surface reflecting golden hour hues

fish_largemouth_bass.alt: Largemouth bass held by an angler

empty_state_fisherman.alt: Silhouette of a fisherman at sunset

instructions_to_main_agent: Adhere strictly to the '1 iOS-Native Clean' personality guidelines. Generous padding, crisp typography, and 44x44pt minimum touch targets are crucial for an outdoor utility app where sunlight glare and movement are factors.
Implement the nuclear ban on all shades of blue. Use the provided Moss Green (brand) and Terracotta (brandSecondary) palette. For informational tags, use Slate Grey (info).

On the Today screen, the hero image ('hero_background') MUST have a glassmorphism frosted panel or a deep gradient scrim (vertical, transparent to >= 70% surfaceInverse) if text is placed directly over it. This guarantees high contrast readability.
Ensure the Barometric Pressure card highlights the trend (Rising, Falling, Stable) using an icon or visual indicator, as this is the most critical feature for anglers.
For the 'Log' screen, implement a sticky FAB (glassmorphism over brandTertiary tint) for 'Add Catch', avoiding bottom safe area collision.
Wire haptics to all primary button presses and tab changes using expo-haptics.
Do NOT use emojis anywhere in the system UI. Use the Phosphor icon set.
